_doc: AGM (Assured Guaranty Municipal) and BAM (Build America Mutual) bond-insurance wrap spread-compression measurement, cross-sector. Methodology: prefer within-issuer / within-deal insured-vs-uninsured pairs (cleanest, no issuer-credit confound); secondary use of named-deal primary-pricing data vs published MMD reference. Reference MMD AAA May 2026: 10Y 3.10%, 20Y 4.10%, 30Y 4.40% (TM3 / Raymond James 2026-05-26).

methodology_notes.preferred_design: Same-issuer same-deal pair: insured maturity vs uninsured maturity priced on same date. Eliminates issuer-quality confound. Used for WCHCC (AGM hospital), Moreno Valley (AGM lease), Brightline Florida (AGM transportation).
methodology_notes.secondary_design: Single-deal pricing scale comparison vs MMD AAA at issuance — measures absolute spread to AAA, not compression vs the same uninsured issuer.

mmd_reference_may_2026.source: Raymond James Municipal Bond Investor Weekly 2026-05-26; cross-checked Tradeweb AAA muni curve.

academic_benchmark_cornaggia_hund_nguyen.paper: The Price of Safety: The Evolution of Municipal Bond Insurance Value, Management Science 70(4):2330-2354
academic_benchmark_cornaggia_hund_nguyen.headline_finding: Pre-2008 average gross insurance value 4-14 bps when insurers carried AAA. Post-2008: 'lack of insurance benefit is attributable to deteriorated creditworthiness of insurance companies' — statistically near-zero average value.
academic_benchmark_cornaggia_hund_nguyen.implication_for_this_measurement: Cornaggia averages across ALL insured deals (mostly high-investment-grade underlyings where wrap is cosmetic). Our finding: compression is highly conditional on underlying-credit distress — near zero for AA- underlyings, 100-450 bps for BBB-/CCC- underlyings.

verdict_framework.VERIFIED: Compression measured at >=20 bps in primary-source matched-pair test for the sector
verdict_framework.PARTIAL: Compression detected but only via secondary design (vs MMD) or very small N
verdict_framework.FALSIFIED: Compression < 5 bps in matched-pair test (= wrap is cosmetic)

cross_sector_pattern.headline: AGM/BAM wrap compression is HIGHLY CONDITIONAL on underlying credit. Compression ≈ 0 bps for AA- and better, ~50 bps for A1 (not directly measured matched-pair), ~135-150 bps for BBB-, ~300-420 bps for CCC-.
cross_sector_pattern.comparison_to_cal_mortgage: Cal-Mortgage produced ~115 bps in-sample / 30-60 bps realizable alpha because Cal-Mortgage was used predominantly on STRESSED CA NH/CCRC obligors (operationally weak credits). AGM/BAM are used across the credit spectrum, so the AVERAGE compression looks small (Cornaggia 4-14 bps) — but on the subset of wrapped distressed credit the compression is ACTUALLY LARGER than Cal-Mortgage (300-420 bps Brightline vs Cal-Mortgage ~100 bps Carmel Valley Manor).
cross_sector_pattern.comparison_to_academic_finding: Cornaggia/Hund/Nguyen 2024 reports near-zero average post-2008 insurance value. Our finding is consistent at AVERAGE level (their average pools investment-grade and distressed) but reveals a strong CONDITIONAL effect: wrap matters most exactly where underlying is most stressed, which is the structural property the masking-mechanism catalog needs to encode.
cross_sector_pattern.implication_for_framework: The 'masking' is asymmetric: wrap converts operator-quality signal into binary insurance-tail-risk signal ONLY at lower credit tiers. Investment-grade insured paper retains operator-quality signal in price (no masking). Sub-IG insured paper (Brightline, distressed hospitals) is fully masked — bondholder underwrites AGM not the underlying.
cross_sector_pattern.alpha_implication: For Signal OS muni-credit detectors: the wrap-masking diligence value is REAL but concentrated. Targets: (a) sub-IG and distressed-IG hospitals (mirror Cal-Mortgage CCRC playbook), (b) sub-IG and CCC transportation/private-activity bonds (Brightline-class), (c) school district and water/sewer paper where underlying is A and below (sub-segment of BAM book). Investment-grade insured paper offers near-zero exclusion alpha.

top_attractive_trades.thesis: AGM (AA) insured CUSIP yields 5.40-5.45% to maturity Jul 2047. Wrap fully insulates from CCC- underlying. Compression vs uninsured comparable: 300 bps. Yield pickup over MMD AAA 20Y (4.10%) = ~135 bps for AA-equivalent paper. Compared to 30Y AA insured muni curve ~5.05%, gives ~40 bps extra carry. Effectively, market is paying ~35-40 bps to question AGM's tail risk on Brightline — but AGM has $13B+ claims-paying resources and Brightline default is a $590M+ claim, well-absorbed. Pickup vs same-rated non-Brightline AGM = ~30-40 bps for accepting tail.
top_attractive_trades.underlying_risk_signal: Pure AGM credit; obligor is masked

top_attractive_trades.thesis: AGM-insured BBB- hospital trades at 4.60-4.77% YTM in May 2026 vs MMD 30Y AAA 4.40%. Spread = ~25-37 bps for AA-equivalent insurance paper. Vs WCHCC uninsured 2052 at 6.00-6.12% (140 bps wider). The wrap fully isolates from BBB- hospital deterioration. The 25-37 bps spread to MMD is in line with general AGM insured curve — fair value, not screaming cheap, but no operator-credit underwrite required.
top_attractive_trades.underlying_risk_signal: AGM credit + tail risk that BBB- WCHCC fully defaults and AGM has to absorb $200M+ claim

top_attractive_trades.thesis: BAM-wrapped TX water (A1 underlying) trading at ~4.98% YTM (3% coupon priced at deep discount 72-73 in May 2026). Compares to MMD AAA 30Y 4.40% = ~58 bps wide. Pickup vs comparable AA insured paper ~5-10 bps; the discount-coupon structure offers de-minimis tax-treatment risk to consider. Solid carry vehicle for retail SMA in a TX-domiciled portfolio (TX has no state income tax so federal-only exempt).
top_attractive_trades.underlying_risk_signal: BAM credit + tail risk of small TX water district (A1 underlying = low real-world default risk)
